title: Grateful Dead Live at RFK Stadium on 1973-06-10

ai_review.summary: Stellar matrix recording that adds depth to an epic 1973 show with a smoking Dark Star, Bird Song and Morning Dew
ai_review.review: Fans rave about Kevin Tobin’s matrix mix, saying it fills the usual dry sound‑board with ambience and clarity while still sounding full. The performance is described as one of the band’s greatest – opening with Morning Dew, delivering an epic Dark Star with a monster Phil jam, and a superb Bird Song jam that keeps the energy soaring throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (8 out of 11) give 4‑5 stars and praise both the show’s musical firepower and the matrix’s sound quality; a few low scores focus on source‑quality issues, but overall sentiment is strongly positive.

recording_quality.technical_notes: The matrix blends dry SBD with muddy audience tape to create depth and ambience; most listeners call it stellar and full‑bodied, though a minority note a slight “cheesy” character when the two sources clash.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Opens with a powerful Morning Dew, moves through jazzy‑jammy territory, and peaks in a third set featuring a monster Dark Star and tight Bird Song jams; the flow is praised as both spacious and tightly coordinated.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work and vocal interplay are highlighted, especially during the jam sections with Dickey Betts, described as sweet and full of “Stellas”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh receives glowing praise for a monster jam in Dark Star, called a rock‑and‑roll god stomping the earth.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums are noted for their clarity and presence within the matrix mix, adding to the immersive concert feel.
